answer.rationale: Finance mandate is hard (18% cut). Only the low-cost vendor's quote meets it alone — and the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so a deferral (c5 logic) would push us onto month-to-month terms with the incumbent at non-mandate-meeting price. Switching is the only path that closes the cost gap this cycle. I'm verifying c2 specifically because that memory claims both sharp unit-cost reduction AND quick onboarding AND accurate invoicing from this same low-cost vendor — exactly the risk surfaces I need to confirm before committing the primary supply line under a tight 14-day window with no buffer stock. c3 (second source) is genuinely attractive as a hedge against the 94% utilization / no-buffer exposure, but I only have capacity for ONE decision this cycle, and the finance mandate is the binding constraint. I'm noting c3 as the intended next-cycle hedge rather than bundling it now, because bundling would dilute focus on the primary switch and likely neither meets the mandate nor fully de-risks supply. I'll also stage c4-style negotiation language (benchmark terms, payment terms) into the switch so we recover additional margin rather than just accepting sticker. Net: switch primary to low-cost vendor under the conditions supported by c2, carry c3 mitigation to next review.
